analysis.title: Coffee Break: 2026 mega IPOs: more value creation happens in private markets
key_insights: Anthropic's IPO on 19 November 2026 was the largest public stock offering of all time, raising a record USD 107.3bn including private placement of shares, above the USD 86bn raised in SpaceX's June IPO.
Anthropic was valued at USD 1.5tn at its IPO and SpaceX at USD 1.8tn. Both are valued above USD 1tn, well above the inflation-adjusted IPO valuations of the Mag 7.
Of the Mag 7, only Meta had an inflation-adjusted IPO valuation above USD 100bn.

Current average price-to-sales for the Mag 7 is below 9x, against 26.4x for SpaceX and 40x for Anthropic. At their own IPOs the Mag 7 averaged about 18x, so the higher valuations rest on stronger expected growth.
Broader stock market valuations as measured by P/E have not risen significantly, while fast-growing companies now go public at much higher valuations than in the past.
Mag 7 shares bought at their IPOs and held to today would have returned an average of 30% a year, against 11.9% a year for the S&P 500 over the long run since 1980.
The author says repeating the Mag 7's post-IPO returns will be difficult from the SpaceX and Anthropic valuation levels, since both already rank among the ten most valuable listed companies.

The author argues the data support including private equity in strategic asset allocation, because early private-market investors captured substantial value creation that they can realise once lock-ups expire.
risk_factors: At USD 1.5tn to USD 1.8tn IPO valuations, repeating the Mag 7's post-IPO returns is described as difficult.
The report says only time will tell whether the SpaceX and Anthropic valuations were justified.
Lock-up expiries will let early investors realise gains.
charts_described: Chart of inflation-adjusted valuations at IPO date (USD bn, left scale) against current price-to-sales ratio (right scale) for Apple (Dec 1980), Microsoft (Mar 1986), Amazon (May 1997), Nvidia (Jan 1999), Alphabet (Aug 2004), Tesla (June 2010), Meta (May 2012), SpaceX (Jun 2026) and Anthropic (Nov 2026). Axis ranges run to USD 1,800bn and 45x.
vol_and_positioning: Lock-up expiries for early private-market investors in SpaceX and Anthropic are a potential future supply event, as these holders can realise gains once the lock-up periods end.

tension_points.bull_case: SpaceX and Anthropic operate in the rapidly growing markets for AI and connectivity, which helps explain price-to-sales ratios of 26.4x and 40x. Mag 7 holders from IPO earned an average of 30% a year.
tension_points.bear_case: At these valuation levels, repeating the strong post-IPO returns of the Mag 7 will be difficult, and only time will tell whether the valuations were justified.

theme_stances.key_argument: Fast-growing companies go public at much higher valuations than in the past, but SpaceX and Anthropic operate in rapidly growing markets, and repeating Mag 7 post-IPO returns will be difficult.
theme_stances.evidence: Only time will tell whether these valuations were justified.
